I farm for yield stability first. I am 60, I have 40 years in the field, and I have well irrigation, so I do not need to gamble on weak seed or very low input management. On 15 mu, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation as the core of the farm because it matches my land, my experience, and the local conditions in southern Hebei. I will put 10 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and keep 5 mu in cotton. I will use better seed on all three crops because I can manage it well and I want stable output per mu. For wheat, I will push for a solid stand, steady fertilizer, and three irrigations because wheat responds well to water here. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer fairly strong, and use no-tillage after wheat to save time and protect soil moisture. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it takes more labor and crop protection, but I will still grow it because it diversifies income and fits my long experience. I will not overexpand any one crop; I would rather run a balanced plan that I can manage carefully with a two-person household.
